summary.thesis: Netflix is a solid, cash-generating business priced below most of its fair-value estimates, but growth is slowing and the price trend is still down.
summary.decision: Long-term: keep adding in small, staggered amounts below the 63.7 DCF base value. Swing: no trade while the price stays under resistance.
summary.act_at: small add below 59.9, next add at 53.74, no buying above 63.7

note.happening: Netflix closed at 58.87, up 1.33% on the day. It is still in a downtrend, below its 20-day (61.81), 50-day (66.58) and 200-day (79.71) averages, and all three are falling. There is no news since the last note. The next report is on 2027-01-19, and analysts have cut this quarter's EPS estimate (earnings per share) to 0.68 from 0.73.
note.business: The core business is still healthy. Over the last twelve months revenue was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Operating margin (profit from operations as a share of sales) rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) grew to 11.4B from 9.0B. The share count fell 3.35% over the year, so each share owns more of the company. What is at risk is the pace of growth. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago. The filings flag a 31% operating margin as the top of its 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like that tend to fade. Debt of 12.7B exceeds cash of 8.2B, which leaves a net debt position of 4.4B. That is manageable against 11.4B of yearly free cash flow, but it is not a cushion. The trimmed estimates (next-year EPS revision of -1.1% over 30 days) and the 3 new risk headings in the annual report affect sentiment and disclosure more than demand. The weak tech market and the falling price trend change the mood around the stock, not the business itself.

worth.text: At 58.87 the stock trades at 16.7 times trailing earnings and 15.6 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 4.9, against a peer median of 6.9, and only the 18th percentile of its own 5-year range. The discounted cash flow model (DCF, which values future cash in today's money) gives 37.99 bear, 63.7 base and 76.06 bull. The company's own price-to-sales history gives 58.94 low, 84.5 mid and 122.15 high. The price sits at or below the middle of every method. The current price assumes free cash flow starts growing about 12.2% a year. At 10% starting growth the value is 53.74, and at 20% it is 80.23. The gap between methods comes down to that growth rate and to whether the 31.3% margin holds. If operating margin falls to 23%, the value is 59.9, still just above today's price. If it falls to 15%, the value drops to 39.57. That puts fair value at 53.74 to 80.23, with 63.7 as the anchor.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% to 20% a year, close to the 12.2% the price implies, and operating margin does not fall much below 23%.
